steps.title: Photograph the bike before you start
steps.instruction: Walk around the bike and take close photos of both sides of the engine: wiring, couplers, hose runs, cable ties, the throttle cables and the clutch cable. These photos are your map for putting it back together. Lay out labelled bags for each area: bodywork, fuel tank, exhaust, intake, electrics, left side, right side and engine mounts.
verification: Photos show every coupler, hose and cable run on both sides.

steps.title: Lift the bike and strap it down
steps.instruction: Put the bike on a solid maintenance stand under the frame so the front wheel is off the ground and the bike cannot roll. Strap the frame to the stand or an overhead point: once the pivot shaft comes out later, the swingarm is no longer tied to the frame.
verification: Bike stable when pushed at the bars and seat.
Front wheel clear of the floor.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil and pull the filter
steps.instruction: Stand a drain pan under the engine. Remove the oil filler cap and the drain bolt with its gasket. Let all the oil run out. Then remove the two oil filter cover bolts, the cover and the filter. Look closely at the oil and the old filter for metal flakes, glitter or chunks and write down what you see.
verification: Filter out; debris noted and photographed.

steps.title: Drain the coolant
steps.instruction: Only with the engine cold. Put a pan under the water pump cover on the right side and remove the coolant drain bolt with its copper washer. Then turn the radiator cap slowly: coolant spurts out sideways, so hold the pan close. When it stops, thread the drain bolt back in by hand so it is not lost. It gets a new copper washer and 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) when the engine goes back in.
verification: Drain bolt back in finger-tight; cap stored.

steps.title: Take off the seat, side covers and air scoops
steps.instruction: Remove the seat, both side covers and both air scoops. Bag the bolts by part.
verification: Seat, side covers and air scoops off.

steps.title: Disconnect the fuel hose and lift off the tank
steps.instruction: Wrap a rag around the fuel hose joint at the tank: there may be pressure in the line. Disconnect it by hand only, never with pliers: slide the connector cover back, press the two release buttons on the sides and pull the hose off. Fit the protective caps to both the hose and the pump outlet. Remove the tank bolts and lift the tank away. Do not stand the tank on its fuel pump; lean it against a wall.
verification: Fuel hose disconnected and both ends capped.
Tank off and stored upright off the pump.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Remove the air filter case cover, unplug the intake air temperature sensor and take off the ECU and the ignition coil so you can reach the harness. Unbolt the rectifier/regulator from the frame. Unplug the generator (stator) coupler, the crankshaft position sensor coupler, the coolant temperature sensor coupler and the gear position switch coupler. Pull the cap off the spark plug and disconnect the starter motor lead at the starter. Free the harness from any ties holding it to the engine; note where each tie sat.
verification: Every coupler between engine and frame unplugged.
Starter lead and plug cap off.

steps.title: Move the rear shock out of the way of the silencer
steps.instruction: Put a block under the rear wheel so the swingarm cannot drop. Remove the rear shock lower mounting bolt and the connecting-arm bolt at the frame, then swing the bottom of the shock to the left. This gives the silencer room to come out.
verification: Shock lower end and connecting arm free; bolts bagged.

steps.title: Remove the silencer and exhaust pipes
steps.instruction: Loosen the clamps between the exhaust sections. Remove the silencer bolts and pull the silencer off. Work the middle pipe section out by turning it as you pull. Remove the two nuts at the cylinder head and take off the head pipe. Throw the head pipe gasket away; a new one goes on at refit. Cover the exhaust port with tape.
verification: Exhaust port covered; old gasket discarded.

steps.title: Remove the air filter case and throttle body
steps.instruction: Unplug the injector, throttle position sensor and intake air pressure sensor couplers. Remove the throttle cable cover and unhook both throttle cables, noting which is which. Loosen the clamp at the throttle body joint on the cylinder head and the clamp at the air filter case joint, remove the air filter case bolts and lift the air filter case and throttle body out. Tape over the intake port so nothing can fall in.
verification: Air filter case and throttle body out; intake port covered.

steps.title: Disconnect the clutch cable
steps.instruction: At the engine end, loosen the clutch cable locknuts, slacken the adjuster and unhook the cable from the clutch push lever. Pull the cable out of its holder.
verification: Clutch cable free of the engine.

steps.title: Take off the shift pedal
steps.instruction: Check that the punch mark on the end of the shift shaft lines up with the mark on the pedal, and add your own paint mark if it is hard to see. Remove the pedal bolt and slide the pedal off.

steps.title: Remove the front sprocket
steps.instruction: Remove the drive sprocket cover bolts and the cover and the drive chain guide. Flatten the lock washer tab. With a helper holding the rear brake on, loosen and remove the sprocket nut and the lock washer, then slide the sprocket off together with the chain.
verification: Sprocket off the output shaft with the chain.
Lock washer set aside to be replaced.

steps.title: Disconnect the radiator and breather hoses
steps.instruction: Loosen the hose clamps at the engine and pull the radiator hoses off the cylinder head and the water pump. Some coolant will still run out; catch it. Pull the cylinder head breather hose off the head.
verification: All radiator hoses off the engine.

steps.title: Remove the engine guard and brake pedal
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard bolts and the guard. Remove the brake pedal bolt and take off the brake pedal and its return spring, noting how the spring hooks on.
verification: Guard, brake pedal and spring off.

steps.title: Take the weight of the engine
steps.instruction: Put a jack with a wood block, or a stack of blocks, under the crankcase and raise it just enough to take the engine weight off the mounting bolts.
verification: Engine weight supported; bolts turn freely.

steps.title: Remove the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove the left and right upper engine brackets with their bolts, then the front mounting bolt, the lower engine bracket and the lower mounting bolt. Keep each bolt with its bracket and note the direction it went in.
verification: All mounts except the pivot shaft removed and bagged by position.

steps.title: Pull the pivot shaft
steps.instruction: Push the pivot shaft out through the frame and swingarm. As it comes out, slide a bar of the same diameter into the swingarm from the other side so the swingarm stays held. If the shaft will not move, stop and check that the weight of the engine is fully supported; never hammer on the threaded end.
verification: Swingarm held by a dummy shaft and still supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out to the right
steps.instruction: Check once more that no coupler, hose, cable or tie still links engine and frame. With a helper, lift the engine and bring it out of the frame to the right side, bottom first.
verification: No wiring or hose damaged on the way out.

steps.title: Put the engine on the bench
steps.instruction: Stand the engine on a bench or engine stand on a clean surface. Plug the open ports. Check the strapped chassis is still steady. Write down the oil and filter findings with the date and engine hours.

critical_stop_conditions: A mounting bolt will not pass through by hand: stop and realign; never hammer a bolt through.
A coupler, hose or cable is left over at the end: find where it goes before starting the engine.
Throttle does not snap shut at every bar position: fix the cable routing before going on.

steps.title: Get ready to refit
steps.instruction: Check the chassis is still strapped with the dummy shaft in the swingarm. Clean the mounting faces on the frame and engine. Have the new sprocket lock washer, head pipe gasket, drain bolt gaskets, coolant drain washer, oil filter and O-ring ready, plus molybdenum disulfide grease and lithium grease.
verification: New parts and grease laid out.

steps.title: Lift the engine into the frame from the right
steps.instruction: With a helper, lift the engine into the frame from the right side and rest it on a jack or blocks so the mounting holes line up. Watch the harness, hoses and frame paint as it goes in.
verification: Engine sitting in the frame with all mounting holes close to alignment.

steps.title: Fit the pivot shaft
steps.instruction: Coat the pivot shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease. Push it in, driving the dummy bar out ahead of it, through frame, swingarm and engine. Fit the nut and tighten it to 85 Nm (63 lb-ft).
verification: Pivot shaft nut at 85 Nm (63 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the lower and front mounts
steps.instruction: Fit the lower mounting bolt and tighten it to 53 Nm (39 lb-ft). Fit the lower engine bracket and tighten the bracket bolts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft). Fit the front mounting bolt and tighten it to 55 Nm (41 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the upper engine brackets
steps.instruction: Fit both upper engine brackets. Tighten the bracket-to-frame bolts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft) and the upper mounting bolt through the engine to 45 Nm (33 lb-ft). Remove the jack.

steps.title: Refit the brake pedal and engine guard
steps.instruction: Grease the brake pedal bolt and a new O-ring with lithium grease, hook on the return spring, fit the pedal and tighten the bolt to 26 Nm (19 lb-ft). Fit the engine guard and tighten its bolts to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft).
verification: Brake pedal bolt 26 Nm (19 lb-ft); pedal returns by itself.

steps.title: Refit the front sprocket
steps.instruction: Slide the sprocket on with the chain already wrapped on it. Fit a new lock washer and the nut. With a helper holding the rear brake, tighten the nut to 75 Nm (55 lb-ft), then bend the lock washer tab firmly up against a flat of the nut. Refit the drive chain guide. Fit the sprocket cover and tighten its bolts to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft).
verification: Sprocket nut 75 Nm (55 lb-ft) and locked by the tab.

steps.title: Refit the shift pedal

steps.title: Get ready to refit
steps.instruction: Check the chassis is still strapped with the dummy shaft in the swingarm. Clean the mounting faces on the frame and engine. Have the new sprocket lock washer, head pipe gasket, drain bolt gaskets, coolant drain washer, oil filter and O-ring ready, plus molybdenum disulfide grease and lithium grease.
verification: New parts and grease laid out.

steps.title: Lift the engine into the frame from the right
steps.instruction: With a helper, lift the engine into the frame from the right side and rest it on a jack or blocks so the mounting holes line up. Watch the harness, hoses and frame paint as it goes in.
verification: Engine sitting in the frame with all mounting holes close to alignment.

steps.title: Fit the pivot shaft
steps.instruction: Coat the pivot shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease. Push it in, driving the dummy bar out ahead of it, through frame, swingarm and engine. Fit the nut and tighten it to 85 Nm (63 lb-ft).
verification: Pivot shaft nut at 85 Nm (63 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the lower and front mounts
steps.instruction: Fit the lower mounting bolt and tighten it to 53 Nm (39 lb-ft). Fit the lower engine brackets with their stamps facing out and tighten the bracket bolts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft). Fit the front mounting bolt and tighten it to 55 Nm (41 lb-ft).

steps.title: Fit the upper engine brackets
steps.instruction: Fit both upper engine brackets. Tighten the bracket-to-frame bolts to 34 Nm (25 lb-ft) and the upper mounting bolt through the engine to 45 Nm (33 lb-ft). Remove the jack.

steps.title: Refit the brake pedal and engine guard
steps.instruction: Grease the brake pedal bolt and a new O-ring with lithium grease, hook on the return spring, fit the pedal and tighten the bolt to 26 Nm (19 lb-ft). Fit the engine guard and tighten its bolts to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft).
verification: Brake pedal bolt 26 Nm (19 lb-ft); pedal returns by itself.

steps.title: Refit the front sprocket
steps.instruction: Slide the sprocket on with the chain already wrapped on it. Fit a new lock washer and the nut. With a helper holding the rear brake, tighten the nut to 75 Nm (55 lb-ft), then bend the lock washer tab firmly up against a flat of the nut. Refit the drive chain guide. Fit the sprocket cover and tighten its bolts to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft).
verification: Sprocket nut 75 Nm (55 lb-ft) and locked by the tab.

steps.title: Refit the shift pedal
steps.instruction: Slide the pedal on with its punch mark lined up with the mark on the shift shaft and tighten the bolt to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Reconnect and adjust the clutch cable
steps.instruction: Hook the clutch cable onto the push lever, seat it in its holder and tighten the engine-side locknut to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft). Set the free play at the lever end to 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in) with the adjusters, then lock the lever adjuster locknut at 4.3 Nm (3.2 lb-ft).

steps.title: Reconnect the radiator and breather hoses
steps.instruction: Push the radiator hoses fully onto the cylinder head and water pump stubs following your photos, and tighten the clamp screws to 1.5 Nm (1.1 lb-ft). Refit the cylinder head breather hose.
verification: Every hose fully on; clamps at 1.5 Nm (1.1 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the throttle body and air filter case
steps.instruction: Remove the tape from the intake port. Fit the throttle body into its joint and the air filter case joint, reconnect both throttle cables to the right pulleys and refit the cable cover. Tighten the throttle body joint clamp screw to 3.0 Nm (2.2 lb-ft) and the air filter case joint clamp screw to 3.0 Nm (2.2 lb-ft); the air filter case bolts go to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft). Plug in the injector, throttle position sensor and intake air pressure sensor couplers. Twist the throttle and check it snaps shut by itself at full left and full right lock.
verification: Clamps at 3.0 Nm (2.2 lb-ft) and 3.0 Nm (2.2 lb-ft).
Throttle snaps shut in all bar positions.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine wiring
steps.instruction: Bolt the rectifier/regulator back on at 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft). Plug in the generator, crankshaft position sensor, coolant temperature sensor and gear position switch couplers until they click. Refit the engine ground lead terminal. Reconnect the starter motor lead and push the plug cap on. Re-tie the harness where your photos show.
verification: Harness routed as before, clear of the exhaust.

steps.title: Refit the exhaust
steps.instruction: Fit a new gasket in the exhaust port. Fit the head pipe and run both nuts down to 7 Nm (5.2 lb-ft) first, then tighten them to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the middle pipe and the silencer with their clamps loose, line up the joints so the clamps do not sit on the locating tabs, then tighten the silencer bolts to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft), the pipe bracket bolt to 20 Nm (15 lb-ft) and the clamp bolts to 16 Nm (12 lb-ft).
verification: Silencer bolts 30 Nm (22 lb-ft); bracket 20 Nm (15 lb-ft); clamps 16 Nm (12 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the fuel tank and bodywork
steps.instruction: Fit the tank, remove the caps and push the fuel hose joint on until both buttons click, then pull back on it to prove it is locked. Refit the shrouds, side covers and seat.

steps.title: Fill the engine oil
steps.instruction: Fit the new oil filter and the cover with a new O-ring, tightening the cover bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the drain bolt with a new gasket at 20 Nm (15 lb-ft). Fill with 0.95 L (1.00 US qt, 0.84 Imp.qt) of 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 motorcycle oil (JASO MA) and refit the filler cap. The final level is set after the first start.
verification: Drain bolt and filter cover torqued.

steps.title: Fill the coolant
steps.instruction: Fit a new copper washer to the coolant drain bolt and tighten it to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fill the radiator with a 1:1 mix of ethylene glycol antifreeze made for aluminium engines and distilled water. The full system holds 0.94 L (0.99 US qt, 0.83 Imp.qt). Refit the radiator cap.

title: Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, cylinder and piston
completeness: Covers taking the cylinder head, cylinder and piston off, measuring every part against its limits, refitting with new gaskets and setting the valve clearance. Valve guide replacement and seat cutting are described as machine shop jobs.
excluded: Valve guide replacement and seat refacing (machine shop)
Crankshaft, gearbox and clutch work (bottom end guide)

required_tools.name: Torque wrench covering 6 to 35 Nm, and an angle gauge or protractor
Micrometers 0 to 100 mm and a cylinder bore gauge

required_parts.name: Cylinder head gasket and cylinder base gasket
Head cover gasket
Tensioner gaskets
Valve stem seals
required_parts.purpose: Always renewed when valves come out.

required_parts.name: Piston pin clips
Access screw O-rings

required_parts.purpose: Only if a clearance is out of spec.

prerequisites: A clean bench and labelled trays for each valve.
critical_stop_conditions: Any reading past its limit: stop and order the part; do not reassemble out-of-limit parts.
A clip or small part drops into the crankcase: stop and recover it before turning the engine.
Timing marks will not line up after turning: do not start the engine; reset the cam timing.
Signs of overheating (blue piston pin, scored bore, seized parts): check the oil and cooling systems before rebuilding.

steps.title: Clean around the top of the engine
steps.instruction: With the engine on the bench, blow and wipe all dirt off the cylinder head cover, spark plug well and the joints between head, cylinder and cases. Grit that falls in now ends up in the bearings later.

steps.title: Take off the spark plug and head cover
steps.instruction: Pull the cylinder head breather hose off and unscrew the spark plug. Note the plug colour and any oil or coolant on it. Remove the cylinder head cover bolts and lift off the cover, the top timing chain guide and the cover gasket.
verification: Plug out and its condition noted.

steps.title: Open the timing access screws
steps.instruction: Unscrew the timing mark access screw and the crankshaft end access screw from the left crankcase cover, with their O-rings.
verification: Both access screws out; rotor mark visible.

steps.title: Turn the engine to top dead centre
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise with a wrench on the crank end until the TDC mark on the rotor lines up with the mark in the cover window. At the same time the timing marks on both camshaft sprockets must sit level with the top edge of the cylinder head. If they point the wrong way, turn one more full turn.
verification: Both cam sprocket marks level with the head edge.

steps.title: Measure the valve clearance as found
steps.instruction: Engine cold. Slide feeler blades under each cam lobe (between lobe and bucket) and find the thickest blade that passes with a light drag. Spec is 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in) intake and 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in) exhaust. Write down all four readings and their positions.
verification: All four clearances recorded with position.

steps.title: Remove the cam chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioner cap bolt and its gasket, then the two mounting bolts, and lift the tensioner off with its gasket.

steps.title: Remove the camshaft caps
steps.instruction: Loosen the camshaft cap bolts a little at a time in a crisscross pattern, working from the outside in, so the caps come off evenly. Stuff a clean rag in the chain tunnel before lifting the caps so the small clips under them cannot drop into the crankcase, then lift the caps and clips away.
verification: Caps off and all clips accounted for.

steps.title: Lift out the camshafts
steps.instruction: Lift out the exhaust and intake camshafts, slipping the chain off the sprockets. Tie the chain up with wire so it cannot fall into the crankcase.

steps.title: Unbolt the cylinder head
steps.instruction: Remove the two small M6 nuts first. Then loosen the four large M9 head bolts half a turn at a time in a crisscross order until all are loose, and take them out with their washers. Three bolts are 135 mm long and one is 145 mm; note where the long one goes. Take a photo of the bolt positions.
verification: All head fasteners out and bagged with their washers.

steps.title: Lift the head off
steps.instruction: Lift the head straight up while feeding the timing chain through its tunnel. Lift out the intake-side chain guide, the dowels and the head gasket.
verification: Head off and on a clean surface.

steps.title: Lift the cylinder off
steps.instruction: Remove the cylinder bolt, stuff a clean rag around the connecting rod in the case mouth and lift the cylinder straight up, feeding the chain and its exhaust-side guide through. Peel off the base gasket and keep the dowels.
verification: Cylinder off; rag in the case mouth.

steps.title: Remove the piston
steps.instruction: With the rag still in place, pick out one piston pin clip. Push the pin out by hand; never hammer it. If it is tight, clean the burr from the clip groove and use a piston pin puller (Yamaha 90890-01304). Lift the piston off. Spread the ring ends with your thumbs and lift the rings off over the crown.

steps.title: Check the valves seal before taking them out
steps.instruction: Turn the head over and pour clean solvent into the intake and then the exhaust ports. Watch the valve seats for a few minutes. Any solvent seeping into the combustion chamber means that valve is not sealing.
verification: Leak result recorded for each valve.

steps.title: Remove the buckets and shims
steps.instruction: Lift out the valve buckets and the adjusting pads (shims) with a suction tool such as the Yamaha valve lapper 90890-04101. Put each in a labelled tray slot for its exact valve and write down the number printed on each shim.
verification: Every bucket and shim stored by position.

steps.title: Take the valves out
steps.instruction: Compress each valve spring with a valve spring compressor (Yamaha 90890-04019) and attachment (90890-04108), pick out the two cotters and release the spring. Remove the retainer, spring, valve, stem seal and spring seat. Keep every part of each valve together and labelled.
verification: All four valve sets out and stored by position.

steps.title: Clean the head
steps.instruction: Scrape carbon from the combustion chamber with a rounded scraper only, keeping clear of the seats and the spark plug threads. Clear any scale from the coolant passages and wash the head.

steps.title: Check the head gasket face for warp
steps.instruction: Lay a straightedge across the gasket face in several directions and try feeler blades underneath. Limit 0.05 mm (0.0020 in). If over the limit, the face can be trued on 400 to 600 grit wet paper on a surface plate with a figure-eight motion, turning the head often.

steps.title: Inspect and measure the camshafts
steps.instruction: Look at the lobes for blue colour, pitting or scratches; any of these means a new camshaft. Measure each lobe height with a micrometer: intake 32.230–32.330 mm (1.2689–1.2728 in) new, limit 32.130 mm (1.2650 in), exhaust 33.850–33.950 mm (1.3327–1.3366 in) new, limit 33.750 mm (1.3287 in). Spin each cam in V-blocks with a dial gauge; runout limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in). Check the decompressor on the exhaust cam moves freely and its pin stands out of the cam.

steps.title: Check the camshaft journal clearance
steps.instruction: Lay the cams in the head without oil, put a strip of Plastigauge across each journal, fit the dowels and caps and tighten the cap bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in a crisscross from the inside out. Do not turn the cams. Take the caps off and read the squashed strip. Spec is 0.028–0.062 mm (0.0011–0.0024 in).

branches.label: Clearance in spec
branches.condition: Every journal reads inside the spec.

branches.label: Clearance too large
branches.condition: Any journal reads outside the spec.

steps.title: Find which part is worn
steps.instruction: Measure the camshaft journal diameter with a micrometer. Spec is 21.959–21.972 mm (0.8645–0.8650 in). If the journal is under size, replace the camshaft. If the journal is in spec, the wear is in the bores, and the cylinder head and caps must be replaced together.
verification: Journal diameters recorded and the worn part identified.

steps.title: Check the timing chain, sprockets and guides
steps.instruction: Look for stiff or kinked links in the timing chain and for hooked or worn sprocket teeth; more than a quarter-tooth of wear means a new camshaft and chain together. Check the intake-side chain guide for grooves or breakage.
verification: Chain, sprockets and guide condition recorded.

steps.title: Test the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Push the tensioner rod lightly with a finger and wind it fully in clockwise with a thin screwdriver. Let the screwdriver go while still pressing lightly: the rod must come out smoothly. If not, replace the tensioner.

steps.title: Check the valve guides
steps.instruction: Measure each guide bore and the matching valve stem and subtract: the clearance limit is 0.080 mm (0.0032 in) intake and 0.100 mm (0.0039 in) exhaust. A guide over the limit must be replaced. That job needs the head heated to 100 °C (212 °F), the Yamaha guide remover, installer and reamer, guide heights of 10.8–11.2 mm (0.43–0.44 in) intake and 11.2–11.6 mm (0.44–0.46 in) exhaust, and the seats refaced afterwards. If you do not have those tools, hand the bare head to a machine shop.

steps.title: Inspect the valves
steps.instruction: Clean carbon off the valve faces. Check each face for pitting and each stem end for mushrooming. Spin each valve in V-blocks: stem runout limit 0.010 mm (0.0004 in). These are titanium valves: a valve that has been lapped must not go back in. Replace any valve that is pitted, bent or worn, and always fit a new guide with a new valve.
verification: Each valve passed or marked for replacement.

steps.title: Check the valve seat contact band
steps.instruction: Paint the valve face with blue marking fluid, put the valve in its guide and press it firmly onto the seat, then measure the width of the band where the blue was rubbed off. Intake 0.90–1.10 mm (0.0354–0.0433 in) new, limit 1.6 mm (0.06 in); exhaust 0.90–1.10 mm (0.0354–0.0433 in) new, limit 1.6 mm (0.06 in). A pitted seat or a band over the limit means a new cylinder head. If you lap a seat, use a new valve for lapping, coarse then fine compound kept out of the guide, and then fit another new valve.

steps.title: Measure the valve springs
steps.instruction: Measure the free length of every valve spring with a caliper. Intake 36.78 mm (1.45 in) new, limit 34.94 mm (1.38 in); exhaust 35.60 mm (1.40 in) new, limit 33.82 mm (1.33 in). Replace any spring under its limit.

steps.title: Check the buckets
steps.instruction: Look at each bucket and its bore in the head. Scratches or scoring mean new buckets and a new head.

steps.title: Measure the cylinder bore
steps.instruction: Look for vertical scratches in the bore. With a bore gauge, measure at the top, middle and bottom, front-to-back and side-to-side, and take the largest reading. New bore is 77.000–77.010 mm (3.0315–3.0319 in); the wear limit is 77.060 mm (3.0339 in).

steps.title: Measure the piston and work out the clearance
steps.instruction: Measure the piston skirt with a micrometer at right angles to the pin, 4.0 mm (0.16 in) up from the bottom of the skirt. New piston is 76.955–76.970 mm (3.0297–3.0303 in). Subtract the piston diameter from the largest bore reading: the clearance must be 0.030–0.055 mm (0.0012–0.0022 in).

Out of spec
branches.condition: Bore past its limit or clearance outside spec: the cylinder must be replaced or rebored with a matched piston and rings; measure the new parts in the next steps.

steps.title: Check the rings
steps.instruction: Clean carbon out of the ring grooves. With the top ring in its groove, measure the side clearance with feeler blades: 0.030–0.065 mm (0.0012–0.0026 in) new, limit 0.115 mm (0.0045 in). Then push the top ring squarely into the bottom of the bore with the piston crown and measure the gap between its ends. End gap 0.15–0.25 mm (0.0059–0.0098 in) new, limit 0.50 mm (0.0197 in). The oil ring expander gap cannot be measured; if an oil ring rail gap is too big, replace the oil ring set.

steps.title: Check the piston pin
steps.instruction: Look for blue colour or grooves on the pin; either means a new pin and a check of the oil supply. steps.title: Decide whether to open the bottom end
steps.instruction: Look over your records. If you found metal in the oil, a damaged crank or gearbox, or the engine is due its major service, stop here and do the bottom end guide now, then come back to the next step. Otherwise carry on.

steps.title: Fit the valves
steps.instruction: Clean each stem end. Coat each valve stem with molybdenum disulfide oil. Fit the spring seat, a new stem seal, the valve in its original guide, the spring with the wider-spaced coils at the top, and the retainer. Compress the spring, set the cotters, release slowly and tap the stem end lightly with a soft mallet to seat the cotters.
verification: All valves in their own guides.

steps.title: Refit shims and buckets
steps.instruction: Oil the shims and buckets and put each back in its original place, number side up. Each bucket must turn freely by finger.
verification: Every shim and bucket in its own place.

steps.title: Fit the rings to the piston
steps.instruction: Fit the oil ring expander, lower rail, upper rail and then the top ring, with any maker marks facing up. Turn the gaps: the oil ring expander gap on the exhaust side in line with the piston mark, the two rails about 15 degrees either side of it, and the top ring gap on the intake side about 15 degrees off the centre line.

steps.title: Fit the piston to the rod
steps.instruction: With a rag in the case mouth, oil the pin and fit the piston with its mark pointing to the exhaust (rear). Push the pin through and fit new pin clips, with the clip gap away from the cut-out in the piston. Check both clips are fully in their grooves.

steps.title: Fit the cylinder
steps.instruction: Fit the dowels and a new base gasket. Oil the bore, piston and rings. Squeeze the rings with one hand and lower the cylinder over the piston with the other, feeding the chain and exhaust-side guide through the tunnel. Pull the rag out before the cylinder reaches the gasket. Fit the cylinder bolt at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Cylinder down flat on the gasket.

steps.title: Fit the head
steps.instruction: Fit the intake-side chain guide, the dowels and a new head gasket the right way round. Lower the head on, pulling the chain up through the tunnel as it goes.

steps.title: Torque the cylinder head
steps.instruction: Clean the bolt threads, washers and the threads in the crankcase. Coat the bolt threads, the bolt seats and both faces of each washer with molybdenum disulfide grease. Run all four M9 bolts in and tighten them in the crisscross order to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft) in two or three steps. Then, one bolt at a time in the same order: remove it, re-grease it, refit it and tighten it to 15 Nm (11 lb-ft), then mark the bolt head and turn it a further 60 degrees. When all four are done, turn each bolt a final 60 degrees in the same order, for 120 degrees in total. Last, tighten the two small M6 nuts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Each M9 bolt went through 30 Nm (22 lb-ft), re-grease, 15 Nm (11 lb-ft), then 60 + 60 degrees.

steps.title: Fit the camshafts in time
steps.instruction: Coat the cam lobes and journals with molybdenum disulfide oil and oil the decompressor. Fill the head pockets with engine oil up to the tops of the buckets. Turn the crank counterclockwise to TDC with the rotor mark aligned. Fit the chain over both sprockets and lay the cams in with their timing marks level with the top edge of the head. Cover the head with a rag and fit the clips. Fit the caps, oil the bolt threads and seats, and tighten the bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in two or three steps in a crisscross from the inside out. Do not turn the crank while doing this.

steps.title: Fit the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the tensioner rod fully in with a thin screwdriver. With the UP mark facing up, fit a new gasket and the tensioner and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Release the screwdriver and check the rod pushes out. Fit the cap bolt with a new gasket at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).
verification: Tensioner bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cap bolt 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).
Chain tight on the front run.

steps.title: Turn the engine and check the timing
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise through several full turns, feeling for any hard spot, and stop at TDC. The rotor mark and both cam marks must line up together again.

branches.label: Marks do not line up
branches.condition: Remove the tensioner and caps and set the chain on the sprockets again.

steps.title: Check the valve clearance
steps.instruction: With the engine cold and at TDC, measure all four clearances again. Spec is 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in) intake and 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in) exhaust.

steps.title: Work out and fit the right shims
steps.instruction: Read the number on the old shim: the number is the thickness in hundredths of a millimetre (for example 148 is 1.48 mm). Round its last digit: 0, 1 or 2 down to 0, 4, 5 or 6 to 5, 8 or 9 up to the next 10. New shim = rounded old shim + measured clearance − the clearance you aim for (pick the middle of the spec). Shims come in 25 types of adjusting pads, ranging from 1.20 mm (0.0472 in) to 2.40 mm (0.0945 in) in 0.05 mm steps. Remove the tensioner and camshafts as before, swap the shims, refit the cams in time, refit the tensioner and measure again. Repeat until every valve is in spec.

Final clearances in spec and recorded.

steps.title: Close the head
steps.instruction: Fit the top chain guide. Coat the new cover gasket with Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) and fit it. Fit the cover and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Refit the breather hose.

steps.title: Refit the access screws and spark plug
steps.instruction: Fit the timing mark access screw with a new O-ring at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) and the crankshaft end access screw with a new O-ring at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the spark plug at 13 Nm (9.6 lb-ft).
verification: Access screws 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) and 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Final bench check
steps.instruction: Turn the engine through two full turns by hand to feel for anything binding. Check every opening is closed or capped and keep the record sheet with the engine.

Squeeze the rings with one hand and lower the cylinder over the piston with the other, feeding the chain and exhaust-side guide through the tunnel. Pull the rag out before the cylinder reaches the gasket. Fit the cylinder bolt at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Cylinder down flat on the gasket.

steps.title: Fit the head
steps.instruction: Fit the intake-side chain guide, the dowels and a new head gasket the right way round. Lower the head on, pulling the chain up through the tunnel as it goes.
verification: Head flat on the gasket; chain pulled up.

steps.title: Torque the cylinder head
steps.instruction: Clean the bolt threads, washers and the threads in the crankcase. Coat the bolt threads, the bolt seats and both faces of each washer with molybdenum disulfide grease. Run all four M9 bolts in and tighten them in the crisscross order to 32 Nm (24 lb-ft) in two or three steps. Then, one bolt at a time in the same order: remove it, re-grease it, refit it and tighten it to 16 Nm (12 lb-ft), then mark the bolt head and turn it a further 60 degrees. When all four are done, turn each bolt a final 60 degrees in the same order, for 120 degrees in total. Last, tighten the two small M6 bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Each M9 bolt went through 32 Nm (24 lb-ft), re-grease, 16 Nm (12 lb-ft), then 60 + 60 degrees.

steps.title: Fit the camshafts in time
steps.instruction: Coat the cam lobes and journals with molybdenum disulfide oil and oil the decompressor. Fill the head pockets with engine oil up to the tops of the buckets. Turn the crank counterclockwise to TDC with the rotor mark aligned. Fit the chain over both sprockets and lay the cams in with their timing marks level with the camshaft cap surfaces. Fit the caps, oil the bolt threads and seats, and tighten the bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in two or three steps in a crisscross from the inside out. Do not turn the crank while doing this.

steps.title: Fit the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the tensioner rod fully in with a thin screwdriver. With the UP mark facing up, fit a new gasket and the tensioner and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Release the screwdriver and check the rod pushes out. Fit the cap bolt with a new gasket at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).
verification: Tensioner bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cap bolt 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft).
Chain tight on the front run.

steps.title: Turn the engine and check the timing
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise through several full turns, feeling for any hard spot, and stop at TDC. The rotor mark and both cam marks must line up together again.

branches.label: Marks do not line up
branches.condition: Remove the tensioner and caps and set the chain on the sprockets again.

steps.title: Check the valve clearance
steps.instruction: With the engine cold and at TDC, measure all four clearances again. Spec is 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in) intake and 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in) exhaust.

steps.title: Work out and fit the right shims
steps.instruction: Read the number on the old shim: the number is the thickness in hundredths of a millimetre (for example 148 is 1.48 mm). Round its last digit: 0, 1 or 2 down to 0, 4, 5 or 6 to 5, 8 or 9 up to the next 10. New shim = rounded old shim + measured clearance − the clearance you aim for (pick the middle of the spec). Shims come in 17 types of adjusting pads, ranging from 1.60 mm (0.0630 in) to 2.40 mm (0.0945 in) in 0.05 mm steps. Remove the tensioner and camshafts as before, swap the shims, refit the cams in time, refit the tensioner and measure again. Repeat until every valve is in spec.
verification: New shim size listed for each changed valve.
Final clearances in spec and recorded.

steps.title: Close the head
steps.instruction: Fit a new breather plate gasket and the breather plate with threadlocker in the threads of the cover, tightening its bolts to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft). Fit the top chain guide. Coat the new cover gasket with ThreeBond 1541C and fit it and a new spark plug hole gasket. Fit the cover and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Refit the breather hose.

steps.title: Refit the access screws and spark plug
steps.instruction: Fit the timing mark access screw with a new O-ring at 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) and the crankshaft end access screw with a new O-ring at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the spark plug at 13 Nm (9.6 lb-ft).
verification: Access screws 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) and 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Final bench check
steps.instruction: Turn the engine through two full turns by hand to feel for anything binding. Check every opening is closed or capped and keep the record sheet with the engine.

entry_state: Yamaha YZ250F engine on a bench with oil and coolant drained and the cylinder head, cylinder and piston removed.
exit_state: Bottom end closed and checked; continue with the top end rebuild and then refit the engine.
title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild the crank, gearbox, clutch and pumps
completeness: Covers removing the clutch, primary and balancer gears, oil pump, generator rotor and shift mechanism, splitting the crankcases, checking and renewing bearings, crankshaft, gearbox, clutch, oil and water pumps, and closing everything up.

Gearbox gear-by-gear disassembly beyond the order listed

required_tools.name: Crankshaft installer pot, bolt, adapter M12 and spacer (Yamaha 90890-01274, -01275, -01278, -04081)
Bearing driver set and a press
Feeler gauge set and surface plate
A strip of aluminium plate to lock the balancer gears

required_parts.name: Crankcase sealant Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) and threadlocker
required_parts.purpose: For the case joint and the listed fasteners.

required_parts.name: Clutch cover, right cover and left cover gaskets
Clutch boss nut and conical washer
Conical washers for the balancer, balancer weight gear and primary drive gear nuts
Lock washer
Push rod circlip, shift shaft oil seal, left case oil seal and drive axle O-ring
Crankcase bearings and water pump seals
required_parts.purpose: Only if worn; removed bearings are never reused.

critical_stop_conditions: The cases will not part with gentle tapping: stop and find the remaining bolt; never pry on the faces.
Crank runout or width outside its limit: the crankshaft must be replaced.
A removed bearing or seal: it must not be refitted.
Anything binds when turning the crank or shifting after closing the cases: stop and open them again before going further.

steps.title: Set up for the bottom end
steps.instruction: Work with the engine on a bench, oil and coolant drained and the top end already off (cylinder head, cylinder and piston), with a rag in the case mouth. Have labelled trays ready for the clutch, the right side, the left side and the gearbox, and take photos as you go.
verification: Top end off; case mouth covered.

steps.title: Take out the clutch
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover bolts, the cover and its gasket. Loosen the clutch spring bolts in a crisscross and lift off the springs and pressure plate. Pull out push rod 1 with its washer, bearing and circlip, the ball and push rod 2. Lift the friction and clutch plates off and lay them out in order. Straighten the staked rib of the clutch boss nut. Hold the boss with a clutch holder (Yamaha 90890-04086) and remove the nut and conical washer; do not use an impact wrench. Remove the clutch boss, thrust washer and primary driven gear, then pull the push lever shaft.
verification: Clutch parts laid out in order.
Boss nut and conical washer set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and filter and radiator pipe 2. Remove the right cover bolts, noting long and short positions, and lift the cover off with its gasket and dowels. The water pump comes off with the cover.
verification: Right cover off; dowels accounted for.

steps.title: Remove the starter clutch from the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Hold the primary driven gear with a sheave holder (Yamaha 90890-01701) and remove the starter clutch screws. Separate the starter clutch, side plate, absorber and starter clutch gear, noting which way each part faces.
verification: Starter clutch parts laid out with their orientation noted.

steps.title: Remove the oil pump, primary drive and balancer gears
steps.instruction: Remove the oil pump assembly bolts and lift the pump off. Straighten the lock washer tab. Wedge a folded strip of aluminium between the teeth of the balancer drive gear and balancer weight gear to lock them, then loosen the balancer nut, the primary drive gear nut and the balancer weight gear nut. Remove the nuts, conical washers, balancer weight, primary drive gear, collar, balancer drive gear, balancer weight gear and collar. Pull out the pin, relief valve and spring.
verification: Oil pump, gears and relief valve out.
Conical washers set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the generator rotor
steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal if still fitted. Remove the left crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. Hold the rotor so the crankshaft cannot turn and remove the rotor nut and washer. Pull the rotor off with the rotor puller (Yamaha 90890-04151) and take out the woodruff key. The stator and crankshaft position sensor stay in the cover unless they need replacing.

steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Pull out the shift shaft with its spring, collar and roller. Remove the shift guide bolts and lift off the shift guide together with the shift lever assembly. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops and remove its bolt without knocking it, because a blow can damage the stopper lever. Remove the segment and the stopper lever with its spring and collar.
verification: Shift shaft, guide, lever assembly, segment and stopper lever out.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain
steps.instruction: Remove the timing chain guide stopper plate, the exhaust-side chain guide and the timing chain from the crankshaft sprocket.

steps.title: Split the crankcases
steps.instruction: Loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a crisscross until all are loose, then remove them and note the three lengths. Lay the engine with the left side down. Tap the splitting rib with a soft hammer, then lift the right case off squarely while tapping lightly on the rib and the engine mounting boss with a soft hammer. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. Tap only on strong cast areas, never on gasket faces. If the halves will not part, look for a bolt still in place; never pry or force. Remove the dowels.
verification: Cases apart evenly; no mating face damage.

steps.title: Lift out the gearbox
steps.instruction: Note where each shift fork sits and which way it faces, and photograph it. Remove the long and short fork guide bars, the shift cam and shift forks 3, 2 and 1. Lift the main axle and drive axle out together, tapping the drive axle lightly with a soft hammer, and remove the collar from the left case.
verification: Gearbox out as one cluster with the forks labelled.

steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft
steps.instruction: Lift out the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crankshaft. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool (Yamaha 90890-04152).

steps.title: Clean and check the crankcases
steps.instruction: Wash both case halves in a mild solvent and scrape off every trace of old sealant from the mating faces. Look for cracks. Blow compressed air through every oil passage.

steps.title: Check and renew the crankcase bearings
steps.instruction: Turn each case bearing by finger. Any roughness, play or rust means a new bearing. Before pressing a bearing out, measure and note how deep it sits. Press it out by its inner race; a removed bearing must not be reused. Press new bearings in by their outer race, square to the bore, to the depth you noted. Refit the bearing retainer plates with threadlocker: plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft). Press a new oil seal into the left case to a depth of 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).
verification: Retainer plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft) and screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft).
Left case seal at 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).

steps.title: Check the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks and measure runout with a dial gauge while turning it slowly; limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in). Measure the crank assembly width across the webs: 55.93–56.00 mm (2.202–2.205 in). Check the timing sprocket teeth and blow out the oil passages. A crank out of limit or with a damaged sprocket must be replaced.

steps.title: Check the gearbox and shift parts
steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface; a bent bar is replaced, never straightened. Check each fork for wear or scoring on its pawls and pin, and that it slides freely on its bar. Check the shift cam grooves and segment. Measure main and drive axle runout with a dial gauge; limit 0.08 mm (0.0032 in). Check every gear for blue colour, pitting, worn or rounded dogs, and that each gear turns and slides freely.

steps.title: Check the clutch parts
steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: 2.70–2.80 mm (0.106–0.110 in) new, wear limit 2.60 mm (0.102 in). Check the clutch plates (1.50–1.70 mm (0.059–0.067 in) thick) on a surface plate; warp limit 0.10 mm (0.004 in). Measure each clutch spring: 46.20 mm (1.82 in) new, limit 43.89 mm (1.73 in). Check the clutch housing dogs and the boss splines for notches or pitting, the pressure plate for cracks and the push lever shaft for wear. Roll push rod 2 on a flat surface; bend limit 0.30 mm (0.012 in). Friction plates, clutch plates and springs are replaced as sets.
verification: Plate thicknesses and spring lengths recorded.

steps.title: Check the primary gears
steps.instruction: Check the primary drive and driven gear teeth and rock them against each other: any free play, damage or past noise means replacing both gears together. Check the balancer gears for wear.

steps.title: Check the starter clutch
steps.instruction: Check the rollers, the starter clutch gear and the damper for wear or damage. Set the starter clutch gear on the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: the gear must lock when turned clockwise and turn freely counterclockwise. Otherwise replace the starter clutch.
verification: Starter clutch locks one way and frees the other.

steps.title: Check the oil pump and water pump
steps.instruction: Check the oil pump cover, drive shaft and housing for cracks or wear and turn the pump by hand: it must turn smoothly or be replaced as an assembly. Measure with feeler blades: inner-to-outer rotor tip clearance 0.000–0.150 mm (0.0000–0.0059 in) (limit 0.23 mm (0.0091 in)), outer rotor to housing 0.13–0.18 mm (0.0051–0.0071 in) (limit 0.25 mm (0.0098 in)), housing to rotors 0.06–0.11 mm (0.0024–0.0043 in) (limit 0.18 mm (0.0071 in)). Replace the pump if any is over. On the water pump in the right cover, check the impeller and shaft and turn the bearing by finger. If the coolant level kept dropping, the coolant was discoloured or the oil was milky, renew the water pump oil seals and bearing; a removed seal is never reused.
verification: Water pump bearing and seals judged.

steps.title: Install the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Coat the crank journals with molybdenum disulfide grease. Pull the crankshaft into the left case bearing with the crankshaft installer pot (Yamaha 90890-01274), bolt (90890-01275), adapter M12 (90890-01278) and spacer (90890-04081). Hold the connecting rod at top dead centre with one hand and turn the installer nut with the other until the crank bottoms against the bearing. Fit the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crank.
verification: Crank fully seated and turning freely.

steps.title: Build the gearbox shafts
steps.instruction: Coat the bores and end faces of idler gears, the collars and the bores of sliding gears with molybdenum disulfide oil. Build the main axle in this order: 5th pinion gear (24T), 3rd pinion gear (18T), Collar, 4th pinion gear (18T) and 2nd pinion gear (16T). Build the drive axle in this order: 2nd wheel gear (28T), 4th wheel gear (22T), 3rd wheel gear (26T), 5th wheel gear (25T), Collar, 1st wheel gear (30T) and O-ring (new O-ring, greased). Fit the washer and a new circlip with its sharp edge facing away from the washer and its ends resting on spline crests.

steps.title: Fit the gearbox and shift forks
steps.instruction: Grease the oil seal lip in the left case and slide in the collar with its slit toward the case. Oil the axle bearings and fit both axles into the left case together. Oil the fork grooves and the shift cam groove and bearing face. Fit forks 1 (L), 2 (C) and 3 (R) and the shift cam: Mesh the shift fork 1 (L) with the 4th wheel gear and shift fork 3 (R) with the 5th wheel gear on the drive axle; Mesh the shift fork 2 (C) with the 3rd pinion gear on the main axle. Screw the spring lightly onto the fork guide bar, oil both guide bars and fit them. Turn the shafts and shift through every gear by turning the drum to prove it works.
verification: All gears select by turning the drum.

steps.title: Close the crankcases
steps.instruction: Clean both mating faces with solvent and apply a thin even bead of Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) to the left case mating face. Fit the oil nozzle with threadlocker at 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Fit the dowels. Put the connecting rod at top dead centre and lower the right case on, tapping lightly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their original lengths and tighten them in a crisscross in two stages to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the gearbox to check nothing binds.

steps.title: Fit the timing chain
steps.instruction: Fit the timing chain onto the crank sprocket, refit the exhaust-side chain guide and the guide stopper plate with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and stopper lever and tighten its bolt with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Push the stopper lever down and fit the segment with its notch over the pin on the shift cam; tighten the segment bolt to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft) without knocking the segment. Oil the pawls, pins and springs, assemble them into the shift lever and fit the shift lever assembly together with the shift guide; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Oil the shift shaft, fit the roller, spring and collar, slide the shaft in and fit a new oil seal.
verification: Stopper lever 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); segment 30 Nm (22 lb-ft); shift guide 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
Gears select through the shift shaft.

steps.title: Refit the generator rotor and left cover
steps.instruction: Clean the tapers of the crankshaft and rotor with solvent. Fit the woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and tighten the nut to 65 Nm (48 lb-ft). If the stator was removed: stator screws with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) (T25), crankshaft position sensor bolts with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft), lead holder bolt with threadlocker at 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft), and Yamaha Bond 1215 on the lead grommet. Fit the dowels, a new gasket and the left cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the relief valve, oil pump, balancer gears and primary drive gear
steps.instruction: Oil the pump drive shaft and inner rotor, fit the dowel pin into the inner rotor groove, fit the outer rotor and the cover and tighten the cover screw to 2.0 Nm (1.5 lb-ft). Fit the spring, relief valve and pin and check the relief valve cannot fall out; it must go in before the primary drive gear and collar. Fit the oil pump assembly and tighten its bolts with threadlocker to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Fit the collar and the balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft spline. Fit the balancer drive gear and collar with the punch marks of the two gears together and the lower spline lined up with the crank spline. Oil the faces of new conical washers and fit them with the domed side out. Wedge aluminium between the balancer gears. Tighten the balancer weight gear nut to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a conical washer and the nut. Put threadlocker on the primary drive gear nut threads. Tighten it to 95 Nm (70 lb-ft). Fit the balancer with its flat lined up with the flat on the shaft, a conical washer and the nut at 38 Nm (28 lb-ft). Check the oil pump turns smoothly.
verification: Nuts: weight gear 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), primary 95 Nm (70 lb-ft), balancer 38 Nm (28 lb-ft).
Oil pump bolts 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft); pump turns smoothly.

steps.title: Rebuild the starter clutch on the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Fit the primary driven gear with its stepped side toward the starter clutch, the absorber with its 5XC mark toward the side plate, and the side plate with its B7B mark toward the starter clutch. Fit the starter clutch with its arrow toward the primary driven gear. Hold the gear with the sheave holder and tighten the screws with threadlocker to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: If the water pump seals or bearing were renewed, fit the new seal with grease on its lip and its marks facing the right cover, and press the bearing in by its outer race. Fit the dowels and a new gasket. Oil the impeller shaft end and mesh its gear with the primary drive gear as the cover goes on. Tighten the cover bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Water pump shaft turns with the crank.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch
steps.instruction: Grease the push lever shaft seal lip, oil its bearings and fit the push lever shaft. Oil the bore of the primary driven gear and fit it, then the thrust washer, clutch boss and washer. Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut, both oiled on threads and faces. Hold the boss with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) (no impact wrench), then stake the nut into the cutouts in the main axle. Oil all plates. Stack the plates alternately, starting and ending with a friction plate, lining up each friction plate tab with the groove. Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1; oil and fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate with its mark on the punch mark of the clutch housing. Fit the springs and bolts and tighten them in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new gasket and the clutch cover with its bolts at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in a crisscross.
verification: Boss nut 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) and staked.
Spring bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cover bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Final checks on the bench
steps.instruction: Fit the filter with a new O-ring and the filter cover. Turn the engine by hand: the crank must turn smoothly and the gearbox must shift through every gear with the shift shaft. Close every opening. Carry on with refitting the top end, then the engine refit guide.
