steps.title: Take out the clutch
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover bolts, the cover and its gasket. Loosen the clutch spring bolts in a crisscross and lift off the springs and pressure plate. Pull out push rod 1 with its washer, bearing and circlip, the ball and push rod 2. Lift the friction and clutch plates off and lay them out in order. Straighten the staked rib of the clutch boss nut. Hold the boss with a clutch holder (Yamaha 90890-04086) and remove the nut and conical washer; do not use an impact wrench. Remove the clutch boss, thrust washer and primary driven gear, then pull the push lever shaft.
verification: Clutch parts laid out in order.
Boss nut and conical washer set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and filter and radiator pipe 2. Remove the right cover bolts, noting long and short positions, and lift the cover off with its gasket and dowels. The water pump comes off with the cover.
verification: Right cover off; dowels accounted for.

steps.title: Remove the starter clutch from the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Hold the primary driven gear with a sheave holder (Yamaha 90890-01701) and remove the starter clutch screws. Separate the starter clutch, side plate, absorber and starter clutch gear, noting which way each part faces.
verification: Starter clutch parts laid out with their orientation noted.

steps.title: Remove the oil pump, primary drive and balancer gears
steps.instruction: Remove the oil pump assembly bolts and lift the pump off. Straighten the lock washer tab. Wedge a folded strip of aluminium between the teeth of the balancer drive gear and balancer weight gear to lock them, then loosen the balancer nut, the primary drive gear nut and the balancer weight gear nut. Remove the nuts, conical washers, balancer weight, primary drive gear, collar, balancer drive gear, balancer weight gear and collar. Pull out the pin, relief valve and spring.
verification: Oil pump, gears and relief valve out.
Conical washers set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the generator rotor
steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal if still fitted. Remove the left crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. Hold the rotor so the crankshaft cannot turn and remove the rotor nut and washer. Pull the rotor off with the rotor puller (Yamaha 90890-04151) and take out the woodruff key. The stator and crankshaft position sensor stay in the cover unless they need replacing.

steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Pull out the shift shaft with its spring, collar and roller. Remove the shift guide bolts and lift off the shift guide together with the shift lever assembly. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops and remove its bolt without knocking it, because a blow can damage the stopper lever. Remove the segment and the stopper lever with its spring and collar.
verification: Shift shaft, guide, lever assembly, segment and stopper lever out.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain
steps.instruction: Remove the timing chain guide stopper plate, the exhaust-side chain guide and the timing chain from the crankshaft sprocket.

steps.title: Split the crankcases
steps.instruction: Loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a crisscross until all are loose, then remove them and note the three lengths. Lay the engine with the left side down. Tap the splitting rib with a soft hammer, then lift the right case off squarely while tapping lightly on the rib and the engine mounting boss with a soft hammer. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. Tap only on strong cast areas, never on gasket faces. If the halves will not part, look for a bolt still in place; never pry or force. Remove the dowels.
verification: Cases apart evenly; no mating face damage.

steps.title: Lift out the gearbox
steps.instruction: Note where each shift fork sits and which way it faces, and photograph it. Remove the long and short fork guide bars, the shift cam and shift forks 3, 2 and 1. Lift the main axle and drive axle out together, tapping the drive axle lightly with a soft hammer, and remove the collar from the left case.
verification: Gearbox out as one cluster with the forks labelled.

steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft
steps.instruction: Lift out the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crankshaft. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool (Yamaha 90890-04152).

steps.title: Clean and check the crankcases
steps.instruction: Wash both case halves in a mild solvent and scrape off every trace of old sealant from the mating faces. Look for cracks. Blow compressed air through every oil passage.

steps.title: Check and renew the crankcase bearings
steps.instruction: Turn each case bearing by finger. Any roughness, play or rust means a new bearing. Before pressing a bearing out, measure and note how deep it sits. Press it out by its inner race; a removed bearing must not be reused. Press new bearings in by their outer race, square to the bore, to the depth you noted. Refit the bearing retainer plates with threadlocker: plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft). Press a new oil seal into the left case to a depth of 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).
verification: Retainer plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft) and screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft).
Left case seal at 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).

steps.title: Check the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks and measure runout with a dial gauge while turning it slowly; limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in). Measure the crank assembly width across the webs: 55.93–56.00 mm (2.202–2.205 in). Check the timing sprocket teeth and blow out the oil passages. A crank out of limit or with a damaged sprocket must be replaced.

steps.title: Check the gearbox and shift parts
steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface; a bent bar is replaced, never straightened. Check each fork for wear or scoring on its pawls and pin, and that it slides freely on its bar. Check the shift cam grooves and segment. Measure main and drive axle runout with a dial gauge; limit 0.08 mm (0.0032 in). Check every gear for blue colour, pitting, worn or rounded dogs, and that each gear turns and slides freely.

steps.title: Check the clutch parts
steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: 2.70–2.80 mm (0.106–0.110 in) new, wear limit 2.60 mm (0.102 in). Check the clutch plates (1.50–1.70 mm (0.059–0.067 in) thick) on a surface plate; warp limit 0.10 mm (0.004 in). Measure each clutch spring: 46.20 mm (1.82 in) new, limit 43.89 mm (1.73 in). Check the clutch housing dogs and the boss splines for notches or pitting, the pressure plate for cracks and the push lever shaft for wear. Roll push rod 2 on a flat surface; bend limit 0.30 mm (0.012 in). Friction plates, clutch plates and springs are replaced as sets.
verification: Plate thicknesses and spring lengths recorded.

steps.title: Check the primary gears
steps.instruction: Check the primary drive and driven gear teeth and rock them against each other: any free play, damage or past noise means replacing both gears together. Check the balancer gears for wear.

steps.title: Check the starter clutch
steps.instruction: Check the rollers, the starter clutch gear and the damper for wear or damage. Set the starter clutch gear on the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: the gear must lock when turned clockwise and turn freely counterclockwise. Otherwise replace the starter clutch.
verification: Starter clutch locks one way and frees the other.

steps.title: Check the oil pump and water pump
steps.instruction: Check the oil pump cover, drive shaft and housing for cracks or wear and turn the pump by hand: it must turn smoothly or be replaced as an assembly. Measure with feeler blades: inner-to-outer rotor tip clearance 0.000–0.150 mm (0.0000–0.0059 in) (limit 0.230 mm (0.0091 in)), outer rotor to housing 0.130–0.180 mm (0.0051–0.0071 in) (limit 0.250 mm (0.0098 in)), housing to rotors 0.060–0.110 mm (0.0024–0.0043 in) (limit 0.180 mm (0.0071 in)). Replace the pump if any is over. On the water pump in the right cover, check the impeller and shaft and turn the bearing by finger. If the coolant level kept dropping, the coolant was discoloured or the oil was milky, renew the water pump oil seals and bearing; a removed seal is never reused.
verification: Water pump bearing and seals judged.

steps.title: Install the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Coat the crank journals with molybdenum disulfide grease. Pull the crankshaft into the left case bearing with the crankshaft installer pot (Yamaha 90890-01274), bolt (90890-01275), adapter M12 (90890-01278) and spacer (90890-04081). Hold the connecting rod at top dead centre with one hand and turn the installer nut with the other until the crank bottoms against the bearing. Fit the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crank.
verification: Crank fully seated and turning freely.

steps.title: Build the gearbox shafts
steps.instruction: Coat the bores and end faces of idler gears, the collars and the bores of sliding gears with molybdenum disulfide oil. Build the main axle in this order: 5th pinion gear (24T), 3rd pinion gear (18T), Collar, 4th pinion gear (18T) and 2nd pinion gear (16T). Build the drive axle in this order: 2nd wheel gear (28T), 4th wheel gear (22T), 3rd wheel gear (26T), 5th wheel gear (25T), Collar, 1st wheel gear (30T) and O-ring (new O-ring, greased). Fit the washer and a new circlip with its sharp edge facing away from the washer and its ends resting on spline crests.

steps.title: Fit the gearbox and shift forks
steps.instruction: Grease the oil seal lip in the left case and slide in the collar with its slit toward the case. Oil the axle bearings and fit both axles into the left case together. Oil the fork grooves and the shift cam groove and bearing face. Fit forks 1 (L), 2 (C) and 3 (R) and the shift cam: Mesh the shift fork 1 (L) with the 4th wheel gear and shift fork 3 (R) with the 5th wheel gear on the drive axle; Mesh the shift fork 2 (C) with the 3rd pinion gear on the main axle. Screw the spring lightly onto the fork guide bar, oil both guide bars and fit them. Turn the shafts and shift through every gear by turning the drum to prove it works.
verification: All gears select by turning the drum.

steps.title: Close the crankcases
steps.instruction: Clean both mating faces with solvent and apply a thin even bead of Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) to the left case mating face. Fit the oil nozzle with threadlocker at 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Fit the dowels. Put the connecting rod at top dead centre and lower the right case on, tapping lightly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their original lengths and tighten them in a crisscross in two stages to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the gearbox to check nothing binds.

steps.title: Fit the timing chain
steps.instruction: Fit the timing chain onto the crank sprocket, refit the exhaust-side chain guide and the guide stopper plate with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and stopper lever and tighten its bolt with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Push the stopper lever down and fit the segment with its notch over the pin on the shift cam; tighten the segment bolt to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft) without knocking the segment. Oil the pawls, pins and springs, assemble them into the shift lever and fit the shift lever assembly together with the shift guide; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Oil the shift shaft, fit the roller, spring and collar, slide the shaft in and fit a new oil seal.
verification: Stopper lever 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); segment 30 Nm (22 lb-ft); shift guide 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
Gears select through the shift shaft.

steps.title: Refit the generator rotor and left cover
steps.instruction: Clean the tapers of the crankshaft and rotor with solvent. Fit the woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and tighten the nut to 65 Nm (48 lb-ft). If the stator was removed: stator screws with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) (T25), crankshaft position sensor bolts with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft), lead holder bolt with threadlocker at 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft), and Yamaha Bond 1215 on the lead grommet. Fit the dowels, a new gasket and the left cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the relief valve, oil pump, balancer gears and primary drive gear
steps.instruction: Oil the pump drive shaft and inner rotor, fit the dowel pin into the inner rotor groove, fit the outer rotor and the cover and tighten the cover screw to 2.0 Nm (1.5 lb-ft). Fit the spring, relief valve and pin and check the relief valve cannot fall out; it must go in before the primary drive gear and collar. Fit the oil pump assembly and tighten its bolts with threadlocker to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Fit the collar and the balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft spline. Fit the balancer drive gear and collar with the punch marks of the two gears together and the lower spline lined up with the crank spline. Oil the faces of new conical washers and fit them with the domed side out. Wedge aluminium between the balancer gears. Tighten the balancer weight gear nut to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a conical washer and the nut. Put threadlocker on the primary drive gear nut threads. Tighten it to 95 Nm (70 lb-ft). Fit the balancer with its flat lined up with the flat on the shaft, a conical washer and the nut at 38 Nm (28 lb-ft). Check the oil pump turns smoothly.
verification: Nuts: weight gear 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), primary 95 Nm (70 lb-ft), balancer 38 Nm (28 lb-ft).
Oil pump bolts 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft); pump turns smoothly.

steps.title: Rebuild the starter clutch on the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Fit the primary driven gear with its stepped side toward the starter clutch, the absorber with its 5XC mark toward the side plate, and the side plate with its B7B mark toward the starter clutch. Fit the starter clutch with its arrow toward the primary driven gear. Hold the gear with the sheave holder and tighten the screws with threadlocker to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: If the water pump seals or bearing were renewed, fit the new seal with grease on its lip and its marks facing the right cover, and press the bearing in by its outer race. Fit the dowels and a new gasket. Oil the impeller shaft end and mesh its gear with the primary drive gear as the cover goes on. Tighten the cover bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Water pump shaft turns with the crank.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch
steps.instruction: Grease the push lever shaft seal lip, oil its bearings and fit the push lever shaft. Oil the bore of the primary driven gear and fit it, then the thrust washer, clutch boss and washer. Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut, both oiled on threads and faces. Hold the boss with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) (no impact wrench), then stake the nut into the cutouts in the main axle. Oil all plates. Stack the plates alternately, starting and ending with a friction plate, lining up each friction plate tab with the groove. Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1; oil and fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate with its mark on the punch mark of the clutch housing. Fit the springs and bolts and tighten them in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new gasket and the clutch cover with its bolts at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in a crisscross.
verification: Boss nut 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) and staked.
Spring bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cover bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Final checks on the bench
steps.instruction: Fit the filter with a new O-ring and the filter cover. Turn the engine by hand: the crank must turn smoothly and the gearbox must shift through every gear with the shift shaft. Close every opening. Carry on with refitting the top end, then the engine refit guide.

entry_state: Yamaha YZ250F engine on a bench with oil and coolant drained and the cylinder head, cylinder and piston removed.
exit_state: Bottom end closed and checked; continue with the top end rebuild and then refit the engine.
title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild the crank, gearbox, clutch and pumps
completeness: Covers removing the clutch, primary and balancer gears, oil pump, generator rotor and shift mechanism, splitting the crankcases, checking and renewing bearings, crankshaft, gearbox, clutch, oil and water pumps, and closing everything up.
excluded: Connecting rod or crank pin replacement (a crankshaft out of limit is replaced as a unit)
Gearbox gear-by-gear disassembly beyond the order listed

required_tools.name: Crankshaft installer pot, bolt, adapter M12 and spacer (Yamaha 90890-01274, -01275, -01278, -04081)
Bearing driver set and a press
Feeler gauge set and surface plate
A strip of aluminium plate to lock the balancer gears

required_parts.name: Crankcase sealant Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) and threadlocker
required_parts.purpose: For the case joint and the listed fasteners.

required_parts.name: Clutch cover, right cover and left cover gaskets
Clutch boss nut and conical washer
Conical washers for the balancer, balancer weight gear and primary drive gear nuts
Lock washer
Push rod circlip, shift shaft oil seal, left case oil seal and drive axle O-ring
Crankcase bearings and water pump seals
required_parts.purpose: Only if worn; removed bearings are never reused.

critical_stop_conditions: The cases will not part with gentle tapping: stop and find the remaining bolt; never pry on the faces.
Crank runout or width outside its limit: the crankshaft must be replaced.
A removed bearing or seal: it must not be refitted.
Anything binds when turning the crank or shifting after closing the cases: stop and open them again before going further.

steps.title: Set up for the bottom end
steps.instruction: Work with the engine on a bench, oil and coolant drained and the top end already off (cylinder head, cylinder and piston), with a rag in the case mouth. Have labelled trays ready for the clutch, the right side, the left side and the gearbox, and take photos as you go.
verification: Top end off; case mouth covered.

steps.title: Take out the clutch
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover bolts, the cover and its gasket. Loosen the clutch spring bolts in a crisscross and lift off the springs and pressure plate. Pull out push rod 1 with its washer, bearing and circlip, the ball and push rod 2. Lift the friction and clutch plates off and lay them out in order. Straighten the staked rib of the clutch boss nut. Hold the boss with a clutch holder (Yamaha 90890-04086) and remove the nut and conical washer; do not use an impact wrench. Remove the clutch boss, thrust washer and primary driven gear, then pull the push lever shaft.
verification: Clutch parts laid out in order.
Boss nut and conical washer set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and filter and radiator pipe 2. Remove the right cover bolts, noting long and short positions, and lift the cover off with its gasket and dowels. The water pump comes off with the cover.
verification: Right cover off; dowels accounted for.

steps.title: Remove the starter clutch from the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Hold the primary driven gear with a sheave holder (Yamaha 90890-01903) and remove the starter clutch screws. Separate the starter clutch, side plate, absorber and starter clutch gear, noting which way each part faces.
verification: Starter clutch parts laid out with their orientation noted.

steps.title: Remove the oil pump, primary drive and balancer gears
steps.instruction: Remove the oil pump assembly bolts and lift the pump off. Straighten the lock washer tab. Wedge a folded strip of aluminium between the teeth of the balancer drive gear and balancer weight gear to lock them, then loosen the balancer nut, the primary drive gear nut and the balancer weight gear nut. Remove the nuts, conical washers, balancer weight, primary drive gear, collar, balancer drive gear, balancer weight gear and collar. Pull out the pin, relief valve and spring.
verification: Oil pump, gears and relief valve out.
Conical washers set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the generator rotor
steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal if still fitted. Remove the left crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. Hold the rotor so the crankshaft cannot turn and remove the rotor nut and washer. Pull the rotor off with the rotor puller (Yamaha 90890-04151) and take out the woodruff key. The stator and crankshaft position sensor stay in the cover unless they need replacing.

steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Pull out the shift shaft with its spring, collar and roller. Remove the shift guide bolts and lift off the shift guide together with the shift lever assembly. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops and remove its bolt without knocking it, because a blow can damage the stopper lever. Remove the segment and the stopper lever with its spring and collar.
verification: Shift shaft, guide, lever assembly, segment and stopper lever out.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain
steps.instruction: Remove the timing chain guide stopper plate, the exhaust-side chain guide and the timing chain from the crankshaft sprocket.

steps.title: Split the crankcases
steps.instruction: Loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a crisscross until all are loose, then remove them and note the three lengths. Lay the engine with the left side down. Tap the splitting rib with a soft hammer, then lift the right case off squarely while tapping lightly on the rib and the engine mounting boss with a soft hammer. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. Tap only on strong cast areas, never on gasket faces. If the halves will not part, look for a bolt still in place; never pry or force. Remove the dowels.
verification: Cases apart evenly; no mating face damage.

steps.title: Lift out the gearbox
steps.instruction: Note where each shift fork sits and which way it faces, and photograph it. Remove the long and short fork guide bars, the shift cam and shift forks 3, 2 and 1. Lift the main axle and drive axle out together, tapping the drive axle lightly with a soft hammer, and remove the collar from the left case.
verification: Gearbox out as one cluster with the forks labelled.

steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft
steps.instruction: Lift out the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crankshaft. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool (Yamaha 90890-04152).

steps.title: Clean and check the crankcases
steps.instruction: Wash both case halves in a mild solvent and scrape off every trace of old sealant from the mating faces. Look for cracks. Blow compressed air through every oil passage.

steps.title: Check and renew the crankcase bearings
steps.instruction: Turn each case bearing by finger. Any roughness, play or rust means a new bearing. Before pressing a bearing out, measure and note how deep it sits. Press it out by its inner race; a removed bearing must not be reused. Press new bearings in by their outer race, square to the bore, to the depth you noted. Refit the bearing retainer plates with threadlocker: plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft). Press a new oil seal into the left case to a depth of 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).
verification: Retainer plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft) and screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft).
Left case seal at 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).

Measure main and drive axle runout with a dial gauge; limit 0.08 mm (0.0032 in). Check every gear for blue colour, pitting, worn or rounded dogs, and that each gear turns and slides freely.

Check the clutch plates (1.50–1.70 mm (0.059–0.067 in) thick) on a surface plate; warp limit 0.10 mm (0.004 in). Measure each clutch spring: 46.20 mm (1.82 in) new, limit 43.89 mm (1.73 in). Check the clutch housing dogs and the boss splines for notches or pitting, the pressure plate for cracks and the push lever shaft for wear. Roll push rod 2 on a flat surface; bend limit 0.30 mm (0.012 in). Friction plates, clutch plates and springs are replaced as sets.
verification: Plate thicknesses and spring lengths recorded.

steps.title: Check the primary gears
steps.instruction: Check the primary drive and driven gear teeth and rock them against each other: any free play, damage or past noise means replacing both gears together. Check the balancer gears for wear.

steps.title: Check the starter clutch
steps.instruction: Check the rollers, the starter clutch gear and the damper for wear or damage. Set the starter clutch gear on the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: the gear must lock when turned clockwise and turn freely counterclockwise. Otherwise replace the starter clutch.
verification: Starter clutch locks one way and frees the other.

steps.title: Check the oil pump and water pump
steps.instruction: Check the oil pump cover, drive shaft and housing for cracks or wear and turn the pump by hand: it must turn smoothly or be replaced as an assembly. On the water pump in the right cover, check the impeller and shaft and turn the bearing by finger. If the coolant level kept dropping, the coolant was discoloured or the oil was milky, renew the water pump oil seals and bearing; a removed seal is never reused.
verification: Water pump bearing and seals judged.

Hold the connecting rod at top dead centre with one hand and turn the installer nut with the other until the crank bottoms against the bearing. Fit the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crank.

Screw the spring lightly onto the fork guide bar, oil both guide bars and fit them. Turn the shafts and shift through every gear by turning the drum to prove it works.

steps.instruction: Fit the timing chain onto the crank sprocket, refit the exhaust-side chain guide and the guide stopper plate with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and stopper lever and tighten its bolt with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the dowels, a new gasket and the left cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the relief valve, oil pump, balancer gears and primary drive gear
steps.instruction: Oil the pump drive shaft and inner rotor, fit the dowel pin into the inner rotor groove, fit the outer rotor and the cover and tighten the cover screw to 2.0 Nm (1.5 lb-ft). Fit the collar and the balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft spline. Fit the oil pump assembly and tighten its bolts with threadlocker to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Oil the faces of new conical washers and fit them with the domed side out. verification: Nuts: weight gear 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), primary 105 Nm (77 lb-ft), balancer 38 Nm (28 lb-ft).
Oil pump bolts 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft); pump turns smoothly.

Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut, both oiled on threads and faces. Fit the springs and bolts and tighten them in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new gasket and the clutch cover with its bolts at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in a crisscross.
verification: Boss nut 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) and staked.
Spring bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cover bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Set up for the bottom end
steps.instruction: Work with the engine on a bench, oil and coolant drained and the top end already off (cylinder head, cylinder and piston), with a rag in the case mouth. Have labelled trays ready for the clutch, the right side, the left side and the gearbox, and take photos as you go.

steps.title: Take out the clutch
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover bolts, the cover and its gasket. Loosen the clutch spring bolts in a crisscross and lift off the springs and pressure plate. Pull out push rod 1 with its washer, bearing and circlip, the ball and push rod 2. Lift the friction and clutch plates off and lay them out in order. Straighten the staked rib of the clutch boss nut. Hold the boss with a clutch holder (Yamaha 90890-04199) and remove the nut and conical washer; do not use an impact wrench. Remove the clutch boss, thrust washer and primary driven gear, then pull the push lever shaft.
verification: Clutch parts laid out in order.
Boss nut and conical washer set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and filter and radiator pipe 2. Remove the right cover bolts, noting long and short positions, and lift the cover off with its gasket and dowels. The water pump comes off with the cover.

steps.title: Remove the starter clutch from the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Hold the primary driven gear with a sheave holder (Yamaha 90890-01903) and remove the starter clutch screws. Separate the starter clutch, side plate, absorber and starter clutch gear, noting which way each part faces.

steps.title: Remove the oil pump, primary drive and balancer gears
steps.instruction: Remove the oil pump assembly bolts and lift the pump off. Straighten the lock washer tab. Wedge a folded strip of aluminium between the teeth of the balancer drive gear and balancer weight gear to lock them, then loosen the balancer nut, the primary drive gear nut and the balancer weight gear nut. Remove the nuts, conical washers, balancer weight, primary drive gear, collar, balancer drive gear, balancer weight gear and collar. Pull out the pin, relief valve and spring.
verification: Oil pump, gears and relief valve out.
Conical washers set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the generator rotor
steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal if still fitted. Remove the left crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. Hold the rotor so the crankshaft cannot turn and remove the rotor nut and washer. Pull the rotor off with the rotor puller (Yamaha 90890-04151) and take out the woodruff key. The stator and crankshaft position sensor stay in the cover unless they need replacing.

steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Pull out the shift shaft with its spring, collar and roller. Remove the shift guide bolts and lift off the shift guide together with the shift lever assembly. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops and remove its bolt without knocking it, because a blow can damage the stopper lever. Remove the segment and the stopper lever with its spring and collar.
verification: Shift shaft, guide, lever assembly, segment and stopper lever out.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain
steps.instruction: Remove the timing chain guide stopper plate, the exhaust-side chain guide and the timing chain from the crankshaft sprocket.

steps.title: Split the crankcases
steps.instruction: Loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a crisscross until all are loose, then remove them and note the three lengths. Lay the engine with the left side down. Tap the splitting rib with a soft hammer, then lift the right case off squarely while tapping lightly on the rib and the engine mounting boss with a soft hammer. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. Tap only on strong cast areas, never on gasket faces. If the halves will not part, look for a bolt still in place; never pry or force. Remove the dowels.
verification: Cases apart evenly; no mating face damage.

steps.title: Lift out the gearbox
steps.instruction: Note where each shift fork sits and which way it faces, and photograph it. Remove the long and short fork guide bars, the shift cam and shift forks 3, 2 and 1. Lift the main axle and drive axle out together, tapping the drive axle lightly with a soft hammer, and remove the collar from the left case.
verification: Gearbox out as one cluster with the forks labelled.

steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft
steps.instruction: Lift out the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crankshaft. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool (Yamaha 90890-04152).

steps.title: Clean and check the crankcases
steps.instruction: Wash both case halves in a mild solvent and scrape off every trace of old sealant from the mating faces. Look for cracks. Blow compressed air through every oil passage.

steps.title: Check and renew the crankcase bearings
steps.instruction: Turn each case bearing by finger. Any roughness, play or rust means a new bearing. Before pressing a bearing out, measure and note how deep it sits. Press it out by its inner race; a removed bearing must not be reused. Press new bearings in by their outer race, square to the bore, to the depth you noted. Refit the bearing retainer plates with threadlocker: plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft). Press a new oil seal into the left case to a depth of 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).
verification: Retainer plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft) and screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft).
Left case seal at 4.5–5.0 mm (0.18–0.20 in).

steps.title: Check the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks and measure runout with a dial gauge while turning it slowly; limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in). Measure the crank assembly width across the webs: 55.93–56.00 mm (2.202–2.205 in). Check the timing sprocket teeth and blow out the oil passages. A crank out of limit or with a damaged sprocket must be replaced.

steps.title: Check the gearbox and shift parts
steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface; a bent bar is replaced, never straightened. Check each fork for wear or scoring on its pawls and pin, and that it slides freely on its bar. Check the shift cam grooves and segment. Measure main and drive axle runout with a dial gauge; limit 0.08 mm (0.0032 in). Check every gear for blue colour, pitting, worn or rounded dogs, and that each gear turns and slides freely.

steps.title: Check the clutch parts
steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: 2.70–2.90 mm (0.106–0.114 in) new, wear limit 2.60 mm (0.102 in). Check the clutch housing dogs and the boss splines for notches or pitting, the pressure plate for cracks and the push lever shaft for wear. Roll push rod 2 on a flat surface; bend limit 0.30 mm (0.012 in). Friction plates, clutch plates and springs are replaced as sets.

steps.title: Check the primary gears
steps.instruction: Check the primary drive and driven gear teeth and rock them against each other: any free play, damage or past noise means replacing both gears together. Check the balancer gears for wear.

steps.title: Check the starter clutch
steps.instruction: Check the rollers, the starter clutch gear and the damper for wear or damage. Set the starter clutch gear on the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: the gear must lock when turned clockwise and turn freely counterclockwise. Otherwise replace the starter clutch.

steps.title: Check the oil pump and water pump
steps.instruction: Check the oil pump cover, drive shaft and housing for cracks or wear and turn the pump by hand: it must turn smoothly or be replaced as an assembly. On the water pump in the right cover, check the impeller and shaft and turn the bearing by finger. If the coolant level kept dropping, the coolant was discoloured or the oil was milky, renew the water pump oil seals and bearing; a removed seal is never reused.

steps.title: Install the crankshaft

Pull the crankshaft into the left case bearing with the crankshaft installer pot (Yamaha 90890-01274), bolt (90890-01275), adapter M12 (90890-01278) and spacer (90890-04081). Hold the connecting rod at top dead centre with one hand and turn the installer nut with the other until the crank bottoms against the bearing. Fit the balancer shaft with its flat side facing the crank.

steps.title: Build the gearbox shafts

Build the main axle in this order: 5th pinion gear (24T), 3rd pinion gear (18T), Collar, 4th pinion gear (18T) and 2nd pinion gear (16T). Build the drive axle in this order: 2nd wheel gear (28T), 4th wheel gear (22T), 3rd wheel gear (26T), 5th wheel gear (25T), Collar, 1st wheel gear (30T) and O-ring (new O-ring, greased). Fit the washer and a new circlip with its sharp edge facing away from the washer and its ends resting on spline crests.

steps.title: Fit the gearbox and shift forks
steps.instruction: Grease the oil seal lip in the left case and slide in the collar with its slit toward the case. Oil the axle bearings and fit both axles into the left case together. steps.title: Close the crankcases

Fit the oil nozzle with threadlocker at 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Fit the dowels. Put the connecting rod at top dead centre and lower the right case on, tapping lightly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their original lengths and tighten them in a crisscross in two stages to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the gearbox to check nothing binds.

steps.title: Fit the timing chain
steps.instruction: Fit the timing chain onto the crank sprocket, refit the exhaust-side chain guide and the guide stopper plate with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and stopper lever and tighten its bolt with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Push the stopper lever down and fit the segment with its notch over the pin on the shift cam; tighten the segment bolt to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft) without knocking the segment. Oil the pawls, pins and springs, assemble them into the shift lever and fit the shift lever assembly together with the shift guide; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Oil the shift shaft, fit the roller, spring and collar, slide the shaft in and fit a new oil seal.
verification: Stopper lever 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); segment 30 Nm (22 lb-ft); shift guide 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
Gears select through the shift shaft.

steps.title: Refit the generator rotor and left cover
steps.instruction: Clean the tapers of the crankshaft and rotor with solvent. Fit the woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and tighten the nut to 65 Nm (48 lb-ft). Fit the dowels, a new gasket and the left cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the relief valve, oil pump, balancer gears and primary drive gear
steps.instruction: Oil the pump drive shaft and inner rotor, fit the dowel pin into the inner rotor groove, fit the outer rotor and the cover and tighten the cover bolt to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) with threadlocker. Fit the spring, relief valve and pin and check the relief valve cannot fall out; it must go in before the primary drive gear and collar. Fit the collar and the balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft spline. Fit the balancer drive gear and collar with the punch marks of the two gears together and the lower spline lined up with the crank spline. Fit the oil pump assembly and tighten its bolts with threadlocker to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Oil the faces of new conical washers and fit them with the domed side out. Wedge aluminium between the balancer gears. Tighten the balancer weight gear nut to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a conical washer and the nut. Put threadlocker on the primary drive gear nut threads. Tighten it to 105 Nm (77 lb-ft). Fit the balancer with its flat lined up with the flat on the shaft, a conical washer and the nut at 38 Nm (28 lb-ft). Check the oil pump turns smoothly.
verification: Nuts: weight gear 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), primary 105 Nm (77 lb-ft), balancer 38 Nm (28 lb-ft).
Oil pump bolts 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft); pump turns smoothly.

steps.title: Rebuild the starter clutch on the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Fit the primary driven gear with its stepped side toward the starter clutch, the absorber with its 5XC mark toward the side plate, and the side plate with its B7B mark toward the starter clutch. Fit the starter clutch with its arrow toward the primary driven gear. Hold the gear with the sheave holder and tighten the screws with threadlocker to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: If the water pump seals or bearing were renewed, fit the new seal with grease on its lip and its marks facing the right cover, and press the bearing in by its outer race. Fit the dowels and a new gasket. Oil the impeller shaft end and mesh its gear with the primary drive gear as the cover goes on. Tighten the cover bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Water pump shaft turns with the crank.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch
steps.instruction: Grease the push lever shaft seal lip, oil its bearings and fit the push lever shaft. Oil the bore of the primary driven gear and fit it, then the thrust washer, clutch boss and washer. Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut, both oiled on threads and faces. Hold the boss with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) (no impact wrench), then stake the nut into the cutouts in the main axle. Oil all plates. Stack the plates alternately, starting and ending with a friction plate, lining up each friction plate tab with the groove. Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1; oil and fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate with its mark on the punch mark of the clutch housing. Fit the springs and bolts and tighten them in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new gasket and the clutch cover with its bolts at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in a crisscross.
verification: Boss nut 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) and staked.
Spring bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cover bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

Screw the spring lightly onto the fork guide bar, oil both guide bars and fit them. Turn the shafts and shift through every gear by turning the drum to prove it works.
verification: All gears select by turning the drum.

steps.title: Close the crankcases
steps.instruction: Clean both mating faces with solvent and apply a thin even bead of Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) to the left case mating face. Fit the oil nozzle with threadlocker at 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Fit the dowels. Put the connecting rod at top dead centre and lower the right case on, tapping lightly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their original lengths and tighten them in a crisscross in two stages to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the gearbox to check nothing binds.

steps.title: Fit the timing chain
steps.instruction: Fit the timing chain onto the crank sprocket, refit the exhaust-side chain guide and the guide stopper plate with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and stopper lever and tighten its bolt with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Push the stopper lever down and fit the segment with its notch over the pin on the shift drum; tighten the segment bolt to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft) without knocking the segment. Oil the pawls, pins and springs, assemble them into the shift lever and fit the shift lever assembly together with the shift guide; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Oil the shift shaft, fit the roller, spring and collar, slide the shaft in and fit a new oil seal.
verification: Stopper lever 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); segment 30 Nm (22 lb-ft); shift guide 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
Gears select through the shift shaft.

steps.title: Refit the generator rotor and left cover
steps.instruction: Clean the tapers of the crankshaft and rotor with solvent. Fit the woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and tighten the nut to 65 Nm (48 lb-ft). If the stator was removed: stator screws with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) (T25), crankshaft position sensor bolts with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft), lead holder bolt with threadlocker at 8 Nm (5.9 lb-ft), and Yamaha Bond 1215 on the lead grommet. Fit the dowels, a new gasket and the left cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the relief valve, oil pump, balancer gears and primary drive gear
steps.instruction: Oil the pump drive shaft and inner rotor, fit the dowel pin into the inner rotor groove, fit the outer rotor and the cover and tighten the cover bolt to 6 Nm (4.4 lb-ft) with threadlocker. Fit the spring, relief valve and pin and check the relief valve cannot fall out; it must go in before the primary drive gear and collar. Fit the collar and the balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft spline. Fit the balancer drive gear and collar with the punch marks of the two gears together and the lower spline lined up with the crank spline. Fit the oil pump assembly and tighten its bolts with threadlocker to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft). Oil the faces of new conical washers and fit them with the domed side out. Wedge aluminium between the balancer gears. Tighten the balancer weight gear nut to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a conical washer and the nut. Put threadlocker on the primary drive gear nut threads, keeping the last 5 to 7 mm (0.20 to 0.28 in) on the outer side clean. Tighten it to 105 Nm (77 lb-ft). Fit the balancer with its flat lined up with the flat on the shaft, a conical washer and the nut at 38 Nm (28 lb-ft). Check the oil pump turns smoothly.
verification: Nuts: weight gear 50 Nm (37 lb-ft), primary 105 Nm (77 lb-ft), balancer 38 Nm (28 lb-ft).
Oil pump bolts 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft); pump turns smoothly.

steps.title: Rebuild the starter clutch on the primary driven gear
steps.instruction: Fit the primary driven gear with its stepped side toward the starter clutch, the absorber with its 5XC mark toward the side plate, and the side plate with its B7B mark toward the starter clutch. Fit the starter clutch with its arrow toward the primary driven gear. Hold the gear with the sheave holder and tighten the screws with threadlocker to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: If the water pump seals or bearing were renewed, fit the new seal with grease on its lip and its marks facing the right cover, and press the bearing in by its outer race. Fit the dowels and a new gasket. Oil the impeller shaft end and mesh its gear with the primary drive gear as the cover goes on. Tighten the cover bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Water pump shaft turns with the crank.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch
steps.instruction: Grease the push lever shaft seal lip, oil its bearings and fit the push lever shaft. Oil the bore of the primary driven gear and fit it, then the thrust washer, clutch boss and washer. Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut, both oiled on threads and faces. Hold the boss with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) (no impact wrench), then stake the nut into the cutouts in the main axle. Oil all plates. Stack the plates alternately, starting and ending with a friction plate, lining up each friction plate tab with the groove. Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1; oil and fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate with its mark on the punch mark of the clutch housing. Fit the springs and bolts and tighten them in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new gasket and the clutch cover with its bolts at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) in a crisscross.
verification: Boss nut 95 Nm (70 lb-ft) and staked.
Spring bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cover bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Final checks on the bench
steps.instruction: Fit the filter with a new O-ring and the filter cover. Turn the engine by hand: the crank must turn smoothly and the gearbox must shift through every gear with the shift shaft. Close every opening. Carry on with refitting the top end, then the engine refit guide.

entry_state: Yamaha YZ250F engine on a bench with oil and coolant drained and the cylinder head, cylinder and piston removed.
exit_state: Bottom end closed and checked; continue with the top end rebuild and then refit the engine.
title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild the crank, gearbox, clutch and pumps
completeness: Covers removing the clutch, primary and balancer gears, oil pump, generator rotor and shift mechanism, splitting the crankcases, checking and renewing bearings, crankshaft, gearbox, clutch, oil and water pumps, and closing everything up.
excluded: Connecting rod or crank pin replacement (a crankshaft out of limit is replaced as a unit)
Gearbox gear-by-gear disassembly beyond the order listed

required_tools.name: Crankshaft installer pot, bolt, adapter M12 and spacer (Yamaha 90890-01274, -01275, -01278, -04081)
Bearing driver set and a press
Feeler gauge set and surface plate
A strip of aluminium plate to lock the balancer gears

required_parts.name: Crankcase sealant Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) and threadlocker
required_parts.purpose: For the case joint and the listed fasteners.

required_parts.name: Clutch cover, right cover and left cover gaskets
Clutch boss nut
Primary drive gear nut
Balancer gear lock washer
Push rod circlip, shift shaft oil seal, left case oil seal and drive axle O-ring
Crankcase bearings and water pump seals
required_parts.purpose: Only if worn; removed bearings are never reused.

critical_stop_conditions: The cases will not part with gentle tapping: stop and find the remaining bolt; never pry on the faces.
Crank runout or width outside its limit: the crankshaft must be replaced.
A removed bearing or seal: it must not be refitted.
Anything binds when turning the crank or shifting after closing the cases: stop and open them again before going further.

steps.title: Set up for the bottom end
steps.instruction: Work with the engine on a bench, oil and coolant drained and the top end already off (cylinder head, cylinder and piston), with a rag in the case mouth. Have labelled trays ready for the clutch, the right side, the left side and the gearbox, and take photos as you go.
verification: Top end off; case mouth covered.

steps.title: Take out the clutch
steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover bolts, the cover and its gasket. Remove the pressure plate 1 bolts in a crisscross, then the spring, spring retainer and pressure plate 2. Pull out push rod 1 with its bearing and circlip, and the ball. Lift the plates and collars off one at a time and lay them out on the bench in the exact order they came off; photograph the stack. Raise the staked part of the clutch boss nut back to its original curve without touching the threads. Hold the sleeve with a clutch holder (Yamaha 90890-04199), remove the nut, spacer, washer, sleeve, absorber, clutch boss, washer, primary driven gear, collar, idle gear and washer.
verification: Clutch parts laid out in order.

steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and filter. Remove the right cover bolts, noting long and short positions, and lift the cover off with its gasket and dowels. The water pump comes off with the cover.
verification: Right cover off; dowels accounted for.

steps.title: Remove the primary drive and balancer gears
steps.instruction: Straighten the lock washer tab on the balancer driven gear nut. Wedge a folded strip of aluminium between the teeth of the balancer drive and driven gears to lock them, then loosen the balancer driven gear nut and the primary drive gear nut. Remove the primary drive gear nut, washer, primary drive gear, collar, starter reduction gear, circlip, starter clutch, balancer drive gear, lock washer, balancer driven gear and the oil pump drive gear. Then remove the oil pump assembly bolts and the oil pump.
verification: Primary drive gear nut set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Remove the generator rotor
steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal if still fitted. Remove the left crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. Hold the rotor so the crankshaft cannot turn and remove the rotor nut and washer. Pull the rotor off with the rotor puller (Yamaha 90890-04151) and take out the woodruff key. The stator and crankshaft position sensor stay in the cover unless they need replacing.

steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Pull out the shift shaft with its spring, collar and roller. Remove the shift guide bolts and lift off the shift guide together with the shift lever assembly. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops and remove its bolt without knocking it, because a blow can damage the stopper lever. Remove the segment and the stopper lever with its spring and collar.
verification: Shift shaft, guide, lever assembly, segment and stopper lever out.

steps.title: Remove the timing chain
steps.instruction: Remove the timing chain guide stopper plate, the exhaust-side chain guide and the timing chain from the crankshaft sprocket.

steps.title: Split the crankcases
steps.instruction: Loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a crisscross until all are loose, then remove them and note the three lengths. Lay the engine with the left side down. Start the split by putting a screwdriver tip in the splitting slot, then lift the right case off squarely while tapping lightly on the rib and the engine mounting boss with a soft hammer. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. Tap only on strong cast areas, never on gasket faces. If the halves will not part, look for a bolt still in place; never pry or force. Remove the dowels and O-ring.
verification: Cases apart evenly; no mating face damage.

steps.title: Lift out the gearbox
steps.instruction: Note where each shift fork sits and which way it faces, and photograph it. Remove the long and short fork guide bars, the shift drum and shift forks 3, 2 and 1. Lift the main axle and drive axle out together, tapping the drive axle lightly with a soft hammer, and remove the collar from the left case.
verification: Gearbox out as one cluster with the forks labelled.

steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft
steps.instruction: Lift out the balancer shaft. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool (Yamaha 90890-04152).

steps.title: Clean and check the crankcases
steps.instruction: Wash both case halves in a mild solvent and scrape off every trace of old sealant from the mating faces. Look for cracks. Blow compressed air through every oil passage and clean the oil strainer.

steps.title: Check and renew the crankcase bearings
steps.instruction: Turn each case bearing by finger. Any roughness, play or rust means a new bearing. Before pressing a bearing out, measure and note how deep it sits. Press it out by its inner race; a removed bearing must not be reused. Press new bearings in by their outer race, square to the bore, to the depth you noted. Refit the bearing retainer plates with threadlocker: plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft). Press a new oil seal into the left case to a depth of 0.0–0.5 mm (0.00–0.02 in).
verification: Retainer plate bolts 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft) and screws 22 Nm (16 lb-ft).
Left case seal at 0.0–0.5 mm (0.00–0.02 in).

steps.title: Check the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks and measure runout with a dial gauge while turning it slowly; limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in). Measure the crank assembly width across the webs: 55.93–56.00 mm (2.202–2.205 in). Check the timing sprocket teeth and blow out the oil passages. A crank out of limit or with a damaged sprocket must be replaced.

steps.title: Check the gearbox and shift parts
steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface; a bent bar is replaced, never straightened. Check each fork for wear or scoring on its pawls and pin, and that it slides freely on its bar. Check the shift drum grooves and segment. Measure main and drive axle runout with a dial gauge; limit 0.08 mm (0.0032 in). Check every gear for blue colour, pitting, worn or rounded dogs, and that each gear turns and slides freely.

steps.title: Check the clutch parts
steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: friction plate 1 2.12–2.28 mm (0.083–0.090 in) new, wear limit 2.02 mm (0.080 in), friction plate 2 2.12–2.28 mm (0.083–0.090 in) new, wear limit 2.02 mm (0.080 in). Check the clutch plates on a surface plate; warp limit 0.10 mm (0.004 in). Measure the diaphragm spring free height: 4.59 mm (0.18 in) new, limit 4.36 mm (0.17 in). Check the collars, pressure plates, spring retainer and the primary driven gear dogs for pitting or wear. Roll push rod 2 on a flat surface; bend limit 0.30 mm (0.012 in). Friction plates, clutch plates and springs are replaced as sets.
verification: Plate thicknesses and spring lengths recorded.

steps.title: Check the primary gears
steps.instruction: Check the primary drive and driven gear teeth and rock them against each other: any free play, damage or past noise means replacing both gears together. Check the balancer gears for wear.

steps.title: Check the starter clutch
steps.instruction: Check the starter clutch for burrs, chips or roughness. Fit it onto the balancer drive gear and then onto the starter reduction gear: the balancer drive gear must turn freely counterclockwise and lock clockwise. Otherwise replace the starter clutch.
verification: Starter clutch locks one way and frees the other.

steps.title: Check the oil pump and water pump
steps.instruction: Check the oil pump cover, drive shaft and housing for cracks or wear and turn the pump by hand: it must turn smoothly or be replaced as an assembly. On the water pump in the right cover, check the impeller and shaft and turn the bearing by finger. If the coolant level kept dropping, the coolant was discoloured or the oil was milky, renew the water pump oil seals and bearing; a removed seal is never reused.
verification: Water pump bearing and seals judged.

steps.title: Install the crankshaft
steps.instruction: Coat the crank journals with molybdenum disulfide oil, and grease the oil seal lips with lithium grease. Pull the crankshaft into the left case bearing with the crankshaft installer pot (Yamaha 90890-01274), bolt (90890-01275), adapter M12 (90890-01278) and spacer (90890-04081). Hold the connecting rod at top dead centre with one hand and turn the installer nut with the other until the crank bottoms against the bearing. Fit the balancer shaft.
verification: Crank fully seated and turning freely.

steps.title: Build the gearbox shafts
steps.instruction: Coat the bores and end faces of idler gears, the collars and the bores of sliding gears with molybdenum disulfide oil. Build the main axle in this order: 4th pinion gear (20T), 3rd pinion gear (16T), Collar, 5th pinion gear (20T) and 2nd pinion gear (16T). Build the drive axle in this order: 2nd wheel gear (27T), 5th wheel gear (20T), 3rd wheel gear (23T), 4th wheel gear (24T), Collar, 1st wheel gear (29T) and O-ring (new O-ring, greased). Fit the washer and a new circlip with its sharp edge facing away from the washer and its ends resting on spline crests.

steps.title: Fit the gearbox and shift forks
steps.instruction: Grease the oil seal lip in the left case and slide in the collar. Oil the axle bearings and fit both axles into the left case together. Oil the fork grooves and the shift drum groove and bearing face. Fit forks 1 (L), 2 (C) and 3 (R) and the shift drum: Mesh the shift fork 1 (L) with the 5th wheel gear and shift fork 3 (R) with the 4th wheel gear on the drive axle; Mesh the shift fork 2 (C) with the 3rd pinion gear on the main axle. Screw the spring lightly onto the fork guide bar, oil both guide bars and fit them. Turn the shafts and shift through every gear by turning the drum to prove it works.
verification: All gears select by turning the drum.

steps.title: Close the crankcases
steps.instruction: Clean both mating faces with solvent and apply a thin even bead of Yamaha Bond No. 1215 (ThreeBond 1215) to the left case mating face. Fit oil nozzle 1 in the right case with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) and oil nozzle 2 in the left case at 1.5 Nm (1.1 lb-ft). Fit the oil strainer with a new O-ring and a new gasket on the left case. Fit the dowels. Put the connecting rod at top dead centre and lower the right case on, tapping lightly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their original lengths and tighten them in a crisscross in two stages to 12 Nm (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the gearbox to check nothing binds.

steps.title: Fit the timing chain
steps.instruction: Fit the timing chain onto the crank sprocket, refit the exhaust-side chain guide and the guide stopper plate with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
steps.instruction: Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and stopper lever and tighten its bolt with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Push the stopper lever down and fit the segment with its projections in the slits of the shift drum; tighten the segment bolt to 30 Nm (22 lb-ft) without knocking the segment. Oil the pawls, pins and springs, assemble them into the shift lever and fit the shift lever assembly together with the shift guide; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Oil the shift shaft, fit the roller, spring and collar and dowel pin, slide the shaft in and fit a new oil seal.
verification: Stopper lever 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); segment 30 Nm (22 lb-ft); shift guide 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
Gears select through the shift shaft.

steps.title: Refit the generator rotor and left cover
steps.instruction: Clean the tapers of the crankshaft and rotor with solvent. Fit the woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and tighten the nut to 65 Nm (48 lb-ft). If the stator was removed: stator screws with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft) (T25), crankshaft position sensor bolts with threadlocker at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft), and Yamaha Bond 1215 on the lead grommet. Fit the dowels, a new gasket and the left cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); fit the oil-tank drain bolt with a new gasket at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the oil pump, balancer gears and primary drive gear
steps.instruction: Oil the pump shaft and rotors and fit the oil pump assembly; tighten its bolts with threadlocker to 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft) and check it turns smoothly. Fit the oil pump drive gear and the balancer driven gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft spline. Fit the balancer drive gear with its punch mark on the driven gear punch mark and its lower spline lined up with the crank spline. Wash the oil off the crank thread, the washer and the new primary drive gear nut. Fit a new lock washer and the balancer driven gear nut. Oil and fit the starter clutch with its maker mark outward, the circlip, the oiled starter reduction gear, the collar, the primary drive gear and the washer. Grease the crank thread, the washer face and the new nut threads and face with molybdenum disulfide grease. Wedge aluminium between the balancer gears and tighten the balancer driven gear nut to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft) and the primary drive gear nut to 170 Nm (125 lb-ft). Bend the lock washer tab up.
verification: Oil pump bolts 5 Nm (3.7 lb-ft); pump turns smoothly.
Balancer driven gear nut 50 Nm (37 lb-ft); primary nut 170 Nm (125 lb-ft).

steps.title: Refit the right crankcase cover
steps.instruction: Fit a new oil seal, circlip and check ball seat in the right cover. If the water pump seals or bearing were renewed, fit the new seal with grease on its lip and its projections facing out, and press the bearing in by its outer race. Fit the dowels and a new gasket. Tighten the cover bolts in stages in a crisscross to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Water pump shaft turns with the crank.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch
steps.instruction: Oil the main axle, then fit the washer, idle gear, collar, primary driven gear, washer, clutch boss, absorber, sleeve, washer and spacer, oiling each part and its faces. Oil the threads and face of a new clutch boss nut and run it on without trapping the washer in the step of the spacer. Hold the sleeve with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 75 Nm (55 lb-ft). Check the washer still turns freely, then stake the nut into the cutouts in the main axle without touching the threads. Oil the collars and plates and refit the stack in exactly the order you laid it out: it starts and ends with a clutch plate, uses the two thin 1.0 mm plates and the seven 1.4 mm plates, and the friction plates with the black-painted tab. Fit the bearing and a new circlip to push rod 1, grease the ball, oil the rod and fit both. Fit pressure plate 2, the spring retainer, the spring and pressure plate 1. Oil the bolt threads, run them to 4.0 Nm (3.0 lb-ft) in a crisscross and then to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new gasket and the clutch cover with its bolts at 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Boss nut 75 Nm (55 lb-ft) and staked.
Pressure plate bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft); cover bolts 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Final checks on the bench
steps.instruction: Fit the filter with a new O-ring and the filter cover. Turn the engine by hand: the crank must turn smoothly and the gearbox must shift through every gear with the shift shaft. Close every opening. Carry on with refitting the top end, then the engine refit guide.

title: First start, break-in and checks after an engine rebuild
completeness: Covers pre-start checks, oil pressure check, warm-up, level checks, the break-in schedule and the service after break-in.

required_tools.name: Spanners for the oil pressure check bolt

required_parts.name: Engine oil and oil filter

critical_stop_conditions: No oil from the check bolt within one minute: stop the engine immediately.
Knocking, smoke or overheating: stop and investigate.
Metal in the oil after break-in: open the engine again.

steps.title: Check before the first start
steps.instruction: Check the oil level is between the marks, coolant at the radiator neck, fresh fuel in the tank, chain slack, brakes and that nothing is left loose. Service the air filter before running. Check clutch lever free play is 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in).

steps.title: Prove oil pressure
steps.instruction: Loosen the oil pressure check bolt slightly. Put the gearbox in neutral, start the engine and let it idle; do not rev it. Oil must seep from the check bolt within one minute. If none appears, stop the engine at once and find the fault. When oil shows, tighten the bolt to 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).
verification: Oil seeped within one minute; bolt 10 Nm (7.4 lb-ft).

steps.title: Warm up and look for leaks
steps.instruction: Let the engine warm up at idle (1900–2100 r/min) and a little above. Look for oil, coolant or exhaust leaks. The engine stops itself after 7 minutes of idling; just restart it.

steps.title: Set oil and coolant levels
steps.instruction: Stop the engine. Wait about 1 minute and check the oil level is between the marks with the bike upright; top up if needed. Let the engine cool, then top up the coolant.

steps.title: Break-in: first 20 minutes
steps.instruction: Ride for about 20 minutes at half throttle or less. Then stop and check for loose fasteners, leaks or anything odd.

steps.title: Break-in: next 40 minutes
steps.instruction: Ride about 40 minutes at three-quarter throttle or less. Stop again and check thoroughly: cable stretch, brake free play, chain slack and spokes. After a new cylinder or crankshaft allow about an hour of break-in; after a new piston, rings, valves, camshaft or gears, about 30 minutes at half throttle or less.

steps.title: Service after break-in
steps.instruction: Change the oil and check the drained oil for metal; metal means opening the engine again. Refill with 0.75 L (0.79 US qt, 0.66 Imp.qt) with a new filter. Recheck every torque point, the generator rotor and stator mounts, the silencer for cracks, and look for leaks. Record the hours.
